solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Approach criminal on the brink

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sitting on another comes first, so the brink follows the criminal

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
the verge is the brink or edge

explanation.surface: A warning to keep away from a crook who is close to cracking.
explanation.definitionFit: To converge is to come together or draw near, so it is a synonym for approach as a verb.

clue.text: Savage, caustic old author taking new lead

indicators.note: the writer's surname gets a different opening letter, swapping its first letter for another

parts.note: Ambrose Bierce, the American writer of The Devil's Dictionary, was nicknamed Bitter Bierce for his caustic wit

explanation.surface: A literary critic's verdict on a bitter writer of the past who has a new starring role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking new lead' replaces the B at the head of BIERCE with F; the clue does not say where the F comes from, so the solver must find a letter that makes a word meaning savage.
explanation.definitionFit: Fierce and savage are synonyms describing violent, ferocious behaviour.

clue.text: Lacking gravity, funny man regularly touring alone

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the alternate letters surround the word for alone
regularly means taking every other letter of the words funny man

parts.note: sole means single, alone

explanation.surface: A comedian on a solo tour whose act lacks weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lacking gravity' suggests weightlessness in space, but it means not serious; 'regularly' takes the even letters of 'funny man' and 'touring' wraps them round the word for alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsolemn means not serious, so it describes something without gravity or weight of manner.

clue.text: Warhol sunk, finally arrested by extremely vindictive sort of fuzz?

indicators.note: arrested by means held inside, so the artist and the letter go within the outer letters
extremely takes the two end letters of the word vindictive

parts.note: Andy Warhol, the pop artist

indicators.note: finally picks the closing letter of the word sunk

explanation.surface: A tabloid line: Andy Warhol, ruined at last, seized by vengeful police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fuzz' looks like slang for the police, which fits 'arrested'; here it is facial hair. ANDY plus K sits inside V...E.
explanation.definitionFit: A Vandyke is a pointed beard, so it is one kind of facial fuzz.

clue.text: Republic overturned denial in one month

indicators.note: overturned in a down clue means the whole construction is read upwards, backwards
in places the denial inside the month

parts.note: Aug is the abbreviation for August, one month
nay is a word of denial, no

explanation.surface: A government overthrown after a refusal in a single month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturned' suggests a toppled regime, but it reverses the whole of the denial placed 'in' the month, read upwards in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyana is a republic on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Criminal also undermining support plan

indicators.note: undermining means placed below, so in this down clue the jumbled letters come after the support

parts.note: a prop is a support

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or wrong, so the letters of also are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook is also scheming to sabotage backing for some scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' rearranges ALSO into OSAL, and 'undermining' puts it below PROP.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposal is a plan or scheme put forward for consideration.

clue.text: Governess expected girl to turn up

parts.note: due means expected, as in a train being due

indicators.note: to turn up in a down clue means the name is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: The governess anticipated that the girl would arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn up' looks like 'to arrive'; in this down clue it reverses ANN to NNA.
explanation.definitionFit: A duenna is an older woman acting as chaperone and governess to girls in a Spanish or Portuguese family.

clue.text: Perform display around north of ancient Greece?

parts.note: to do is to perform

indicators.note: around means turned round, so the word for display is reversed

parts.note: to air is to display, as in airing views

explanation.surface: An instruction to stage a show about the northern part of old Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'north of ancient Greece' reads as a region, but north only supplies N; 'around' turns the word for display backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorians were one of the main peoples of ancient Greece, so the adjective names something belonging to that world.

clue.text: Sign almost marks where submerged activity may be seen

definitions.text: where submerged activity may be seen

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: Aquarius is a sign of the zodiac
M was an abbreviation for marks, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A signal that is nearly a mark of hidden goings-on underwater.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims the S from AQUARIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A fish tank lets people watch life under the water, a cryptic description of the place.

clue.text: Tax charge on deliveries

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece on another follows it, so the charge comes after the deliveries

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six deliveries bowled
a load is a charge or burden

explanation.surface: A levy imposed on goods being delivered.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is six balls bowled by one bowler, so 'deliveries' gives OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To overload is to burden too heavily, which is one sense of tax as a verb.

clue.text: ID carried by former fighter in high-up troops

indicators.note: carried by means held inside, so the identification goes within the boxer

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, the late heavyweight boxer
a PIN, personal identification number, is a form of ID

explanation.surface: An old soldier carrying identification among mountain soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: Muhammad Ali was the heavyweight boxing champion; his name holds PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Alpini are Italian mountain infantry, soldiers who serve at altitude.

clue.text: Young English Catholic novelist

parts.note: green means young and inexperienced

explanation.surface: A description of a youthful English writer of Catholic faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Graham Greene was a Catholic convert whose novels such as Brighton Rock explore faith.

clue.text: Supremacist response curtailed in airline article

indicators.note: in places the shortened response inside the airline's code

parts.note: KLM is the Dutch national airline

indicators.note: curtailed means cut short at the tail, so the end of the word for response is dropped

parts.note: an answer is a response
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A shortened reply printed in a feature in an in-flight magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: The airline is Royal Dutch Airlines, known by its initials; 'curtailed' cuts the tail off the response, and 'in' sets what is left between the airline's last two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Ku Klux Klan holds white supremacist views.

clue.text: Daughter stops dating, sorting out better players

indicators.note: stops means plugs a gap, so the abbreviation sits inside the word for dating

parts.note: seeing someone means dating them

explanation.surface: A daughter ends a relationship while weighing up better suitors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorting out better players' sounds like choosing partners; it is the ranking of top players in a tournament draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeding ranks the strongest competitors so they are kept apart in the early rounds of a tournament.

clue.text: Heard dog barking in a port

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters of heard dog are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone hears a dog barking in a harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' looks literal for a dog; it is British slang for mad, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Drogheda is a port town on the east coast of Ireland, on the River Boyne.

clue.text: Using post, distribute tights

parts.note: post and mail are synonyms
to lot is to divide into portions, to distribute

explanation.surface: An instruction to send out hosiery by mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A maillot is a pair of tights worn by dancers, also a one-piece swimsuit.

clue.text: Don's half cutting bills

definitions.note: Don's stands for Don is, and the definition is the noun don, a university lecturer

indicators.note: cutting means slicing into, so the half goes inside the bills

parts.note: ac is the abbreviation for account, a bill; two of them make the plural
demi is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: A man named Don has halved his bills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Don's' is 'Don is' with a hidden capital: a don is a lecturer. Two ACs, accounts, are split by DEMI.
explanation.definitionFit: A don is a university teacher, a scholar working in academia.

clue.text: You and I sold out in a hateful way

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so the letters of you, I and sold are mixed up

explanation.surface: An accusation that the two of us betrayed someone nastily.
explanation.definitionFit: Odious means hateful or repugnant, so the adverb describes acting in a hateful manner.

clue.text: For each climbing record, a climber may climb this

parts.note: per means for each, as in a pound per head

indicators.note: climbing in a down clue means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a log is a record, as kept on a ship

explanation.surface: A note on how a climbing plant scales a garden frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses LOG to GOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pergola is a framework of posts and beams over which climbing plants grow.

clue.text: Valve that's half dry in part

indicators.note: half takes the first two of the four letters of the word that
in puts the teetotal letters inside the word for part

parts.note: a role is an actor's part
TT means teetotal, so dry in the sense of not drinking

explanation.surface: A valve described as half dry inside one part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's half' means the first half of the word 'that'; TT, teetotal, is the usual crossword shorthand for dry, and 'in' sets it inside an actor's part.
explanation.definitionFit: A throttle is a valve controlling the flow of fuel or steam to an engine.

clue.text: Hungry hippo, extremely large and depressed

indicators.note: extremely takes the two end letters of the word hippo

parts.note: low means depressed, down in spirits

explanation.surface: A hippo that is starving, huge and gloomy, like the children's game Hungry Hippos.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel hollow is to feel empty inside, hungry for food.

clue.text: Kids regularly chasing match ball

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the alternate letters follow the match

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: regularly takes alternate letters of the word kids

explanation.surface: Children running after the ball at a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test match is an international cricket fixture; 'ball' is not the cricket ball but slang for a testicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A testis is a testicle, which is called a ball in slang.

clue.text: Inability to read law stopping excellent start for 17

indicators.note: stopping means plugging, so the law sits inside the word for excellent

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as AI
lex is Latin for law
the first letter of the answer to 17 down

explanation.surface: A legal obstacle to reading, an excellent beginning for a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: A1, first-rate, is written AI with the figure one as I; 17 down is ACADEMIC, so its start is A.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexia is a neurological condition in which a person loses the ability to read.

clue.text: Legally precludes unnamed stepson for beating

indicators.note: beating means battered out of shape, so the remaining letters are rearranged
unnamed means without N, the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A stepson, anonymous, threatened with a thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unnamed' removes N from STEPSON, and 'for beating' rearranges STEPSO.
explanation.definitionFit: To estop is to bar someone in law from asserting something contrary to what they said or did before.

clue.text: Dominant group in area left stage briefly

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a phase is a stage

explanation.surface: Top dogs in some district quickly left the platform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' drops the E of PHASE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alpha animals or people are the dominant members of their group.

clue.text: Said dismal king trapping foreign character, one who was grounded

indicators.note: trapping means holding inside, so the Greek letter goes within
said means spoken, so the word for dismal is given by how it is pronounced

parts.note: grey means dull and dismal
K is the abbreviation for king in chess
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A gloomy monarch is reported to have captured an alien.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one who was grounded' is a bird that could not fly and is now extinct.
explanation.definitionFit: The great auk was a large flightless seabird, hunted to extinction in the 1840s.

clue.text: Scoff on the way

parts.note: scoff is slang for food, and food found lying on the road is animals hit by traffic

explanation.surface: A snack eaten while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals killed by vehicles lie on the road and are jokingly treated as free food found en route.

clue.text: The beast of Blenheim Palace?

indicators.note: of signals the letters are taken from within the words Blenheim Palace

explanation.surface: A question about which animal lives at Blenheim Palace, the Oxfordshire stately home.
explanation.definitionFit: An impala is an African antelope, a wild animal.
